app.title: SiOC/SiOCN Battery Anode Designer
app.summary: A person enters a target material design in the sidebar: element weight percentages, final processing temperature and time, and a cycle number. They can also add a measured surface area or a measured first result. The interface predicts several performance values with trained models, works out a derived loss and a retention ratio from them, and checks each input against the range the models were trained on. It warns when a design lies outside that range. Tabs then show the phase descriptors derived from the composition, synthesis routes ranked by how closely their composition matches, the nearest published examples with links to their sources, and the models' cross-validation results. The person comes away with a predicted performance profile for a candidate design and a route to try making it.

task.text: Predict how a candidate material will perform from its composition and processing before anyone makes it, check whether the prediction falls inside the model's training range, and find published routes that could produce it.

data.text: A single designed material, entered as element fractions and processing conditions, checked against a reference table of published samples. Each sample in that table has a composition, processing conditions, measured performance and a source DOI. The precursor families are a fixed set of named categories with descriptions.
data.item: one candidate material design: element weight fractions plus processing temperature and time

stage.text: screening candidate material designs by predicted performance before synthesis

mechanism.text: Inputs in the sidebar feed the trained models on every change. Prediction cards and range checks sit side by side so each value is read together with its training-range status. Tabs below show the same design from other sides: where the prediction falls in the training distribution, the phase descriptors derived from the composition, a table of composition-matched routes filtered by a match-threshold slider, and the nearest published analogs with DOI links.

field.text: predicting material properties from composition and processing with machine learning, in materials informatics

workflow.name: predict the properties of a designed item and find precedents for making it

steps.here: Number inputs for each element's weight percentage, processing temperature and time, and a cycle-number choice. A warning appears when the composition does not sum to 100 or falls outside the training range. Optional expanders switch on a model that uses a measured surface area, or one that uses a measured first result.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Trained models predict first-cycle capacity, efficiency and cycled capacity. Irreversible loss is calculated from the first two, retention as the ratio of cycled to first capacity, and cycled capacity is capped so it never rises with cycle number. Results are shown as cards, with a comparison to a standard reference material.

steps.step: check whether the result can be trusted
steps.here: Each input is marked as inside or outside the model's training range, with the full range and the common 5–95% range. A histogram shows where the prediction falls in the training distribution, next to the exact feature matrix sent to the model.

steps.step: inspect derived descriptors of the item
steps.here: The composition is turned into phase-fraction progress bars, normalized phase percentages and three formula pills, followed by the feature tables grouped by kind.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Two sliders set how many nearby published samples to search and the minimum family-match percentage. Matching samples are grouped by precursor family and modifier into ranked recipe rows with a confidence level, and the top recipe idea is spelled out.

Published samples are ranked by composition distance and listed with their processing, performance and a clickable DOI. The search is limited to nitrogen-containing samples when the target contains nitrogen.

steps.step: review how well the model was validated
steps.here: The Model Results tab lists each model bundle with its estimator and features, and compares grouped against shuffled cross-validation error. A Tips and Limits tab states which inputs the models use and which they ignore.

distinctive: Inputs may go beyond the training data on purpose, for discovery. Every value is marked inside or outside the training range rather than clamped.
Some predictions can use a predicted first result or a measured one, so the same screen serves both virtual screening before an experiment and diagnosis after it.
Route suggestions match on composition only and are kept apart from the prediction: choosing a precursor never changes the predicted values.
Cross-validation groups samples by source paper, so samples from the same paper never land in both training and test folds. A shuffled split is shown only as an optimistic comparison.
Derived quantities follow physical rules: loss is calculated from capacity and efficiency, and cycled capacity is capped so it does not rise with cycle number.
